pattern-selector.why: the change audits this skill's own catalog against Fowler's PoEAA and specifies its v1.4 fixes; the audit tested the skill's claim that its gate keeps the catalog honest and found it does not check citation correctness.
pattern-selector.what: scored all 51 PoEAA patterns against the catalog, mutation-tested check-catalog-completeness.mjs, and specified the page registry, the corrected entries, the new entries, and the prove-it kit.
quotes: chooses from can be kept honest, and it must be, because every other skill here ships a gate.

architectural-decision-records.why: making the pattern skills true to PoEAA in v1.4, gate first, as nine serial work packages with a single-owner page registry, is a significant lasting decision with rejected alternatives.
architectural-decision-records.what: wrote ADR-0103 with context, decision, consequences, and five rejected alternatives; validated it with check_adr.sh.
quotes: Every architecturally significant change ships with an ADR in the same unit of work

bdd-comprehensive-testing.why: every audit finding needs readable acceptance scenarios; because the repo gates execution of every scenario in features/, unbuilt behavior is specified under docs/design/ and graduates with its step definitions.
bdd-comprehensive-testing.what: wrote 9 system feature files (52 scenarios, 96 outline rows, 148 cases) and 1 eval file (11 scenarios), all passing check-gherkin-valid and check-bdd-tags; a planted bad tag made the tag gate exit 1.
quotes: files and go green while no behavior was ever exercised

comprehensive-test-strategy.why: the prove-it half of the audit needs a test shape per pattern beyond grep rules, and the spec splits deterministic system tests from agent-behavior evals that cannot be a pass or fail step.
comprehensive-test-strategy.what: specified named test shapes for Unit of Work, Identity Map, Optimistic Offline Lock, Lazy Load, DTO, Money and Special Case, and a requirement that comprehensive-test-strategy link to the kit.
quotes: checker that decides pass or fail but is itself wrong

verifiable-quality-gates.why: the central finding is a gate that cannot detect what it claims; the audit proved it by mutation, and the spec requires the replacement gate and every kit rule to ship a discriminating test.
verifiable-quality-gates.what: ran four mutated catalog copies through check-catalog-completeness.mjs (all exit 0); planted an em dash to prove the widened house-style include fires; specified R2.8 and R9.2 discriminating tests.
quotes: A test that runs the check but asserts nothing tied to detection would let a broken check ship green.

skeptical-audit.why: the deliverable is an audit made of factual claims about a book and a repo, each needing an evidence state, a re-runnable source, and a named limit.
skeptical-audit.what: evidence ledger in the report; every book quote re-found in the extracted text by script (caught four wrong PDF pages in the first draft); claim-lint --strict run clean on all five prose files.
quotes: Before you hit send, scan your own draft for the banned moves above.

judge-arch.why: the change restructures no code but adds a gate-config edit and a design that later PRs build on, so it gets a fresh-context review recorded in the log before it is called done.
judge-arch.what: dispatched a fresh-context subagent review over every changed file and the four questions (9 findings: 0 high, 5 med, 4 low); fixed all nine in the same change; recorded the review and the resolutions in docs/arch-reviews/log.jsonl; npm run check:architecture exits 0.
quotes: Review from a blank slate, never from the conversation that wrote the code.

release-deployment-safety.why: documentation and a house-style config include only; nothing is deployed, released, or migrated, and no runtime behavior changes.

enterprise-architecture-standards.why: the audit covers this skill's references that overlap PoEAA (session state, N+1, keys), and the spec's design keeps one owner for page facts and avoids building beyond the findings.
enterprise-architecture-standards.what: audited database-architecture.md, performance-scalability.md, microservices-patterns.md and api-integration-design.md for PoEAA gaps (F12, F14); specified R4.8; kept the registry as the single owner of page facts.
quotes: Simplicity that meets the real requirement is a core principle, not a shortcut.

owasp-secure-coding-bdd.why: concurrency-and-session.feature specifies the Client Session State entry, a security surface: state held by the client can be read and changed by the client. The threat is tampering (STRIDE T) and elevation of privilege when that state decides access.
owasp-secure-coding-bdd.what: mapped the threat to the Insecure_Direct_Object_Reference_Prevention and JSON_Web_Token cheat sheets; the scenario now requires the structural control first (data that decides access stays on the server), then signing or encrypting client-held state and verifying it on every request, as anchored Thens tagged @quality:security for WP5.
quotes: A threat with no countermeasure is a vulnerability, not a decision.

compliance-data-lifecycle.why: no personal or regulated data is stored, moved, or deleted by this change; the Serialized LOB personal-data caveat is carried into the spec for the work package that builds that entry.

sre-operational-readiness.why: no service, endpoint, or production system is added or changed.

arch-encode.why: the no-dash house rule is checkable, so the new audit and design folders are wired into the mechanical gate instead of relying on prose.
arch-encode.what: added docs/audit/poeaa-2026-11, docs/design/poeaa-v1.4 (md and feature), and ADR-0103 to house-style-no-em-dash; proved it by planting an em dash (exit 1) and removing it.
quotes: A rule that can be mechanical should be.

universal-accessibility-wcag.why: no UI is rendered or changed.

usability-ux-universal-design.why: the operator asked for the findings in plain English at a 7th-grade reading level, which is this skill's content guidance and its readability gate.
usability-ux-universal-design.what: wrote plain-english-summary.md and gated it with readability.mjs --max-grade 7 (measured grade 4, exit 0).
quotes: Words are UI, and people skim rather than read:
